A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Policy Contrastive Decoding (PCD) work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching, including retained material that moves within the appendices.

before.justification: v3 reports original SIMPLER experiments, six real-world manipulation tasks, ablations, robustness tests, and computational measurements, including Table 1 and Figures 3–5.

after.justification: v5 retains those original results and adds CFG comparisons, masking and distractor experiments, and evaluation on five LIBERO-90 tasks in Appendices F–K.

M1.justification: The contrastive policy equation, Track2Mask, KDE-based probability modeling, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Appendix H explains masking choices for existing multi-object and sequential tasks; it does not establish a revision to the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix K adds five LIBERO-90 tasks evaluated with both third-person and wrist observations, extending benchmark coverage and input conditions beyond v3's SIMPLER and real-world evaluations. Appendix J also adds graduated background-distractor scenarios. The complex tasks discussed in Appendix H were already present.

E2.justification: Table 6 introduces classifier-free guidance (CFG) as an evaluated alternative to PCD on π0 across nine SIMPLER tasks. Table 11 adds miniVLA+VQ h8+Wrist as a baseline policy. These substantially extend comparison beyond v3's retained OpenVLA, Octo, and π0 evaluations.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs vary CFG starting steps, manually exclude different fractions of masked pixels, and compare four object-masking schedules. Appendix K specifies five randomly sampled LIBERO-90 tasks and a multi-view policy configuration. The original simulation and real-world protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices F–J add substantial diagnostics: CFG intervention timing, detection and incomplete-masking failures, multi-object masking choices, annotation-dependent masking examples, and sensitivity to distractor quantity. These test additional mechanisms and failure conditions beyond v3's hyperparameter, detector, inpainting, and scene-shift analyses.

E5.justification: Appendix F newly specifies 100 trials per CFG starting-step setting, adding repetition information without establishing increased runs for retained experiments. Existing 95% confidence intervals in Tables 1 and 4 remain unchanged; the new tables report point estimates without additional uncertainty estimates or significance tests.

E6.justification: Original results remain unchanged, while Tables 6–11 add substantial findings. Table 6 adds CFG's 62.7% average alongside the retained 68.1% PCD Point result. Table 8 reports masking-related degradation, and Table 11 reports 71.2% for miniVLA versus 79.6% with PCD. These are additional comparisons, not improved versions of the original benchmark scores.

T1.justification: Definition 3.1, Equations (1)–(3), and the action-dimension independence assumption are unchanged. The new CFG discussion and explanation of baseline-equivalent predictions when detection fails introduce no new formal derivation, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same training-free, plug-and-play contributions, three-policy and 15-task framing, and headline improvements of 8.9% in simulation and 108% in real-world evaluation. New appendix evidence does not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: Appendices F–I add a hypothesized explanation for CFG degradation, identify detection and incomplete-masking failure conditions, and qualify annotation effectiveness as task dependent. They also explain subtask-specific masking and suggest future LLM-based planning for longer tasks. These materially expand v3's interpretations and applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: Appendix H newly documents simultaneous masking of relevant objects and the masks used for each Apple Drawer subtask. Appendix F describes masked-image conditioning for CFG, and the project-page address changes. Existing fine-tuning hyperparameters, model-access references, and computational details are retained.

R1.justification: v5 adds references to CFG, miniVLA, and Inspire. Appendix F distinguishes PCD's explicit post-hoc correction from CFG's iterative guidance. This is a focused positioning extension; the main related-work discussion, VCD inspiration, and novelty framing remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The retained scientific narrative is nearly verbatim, with localized wording changes, revised author and publication-status text, and an added acknowledgment. New appendix sections precede the unchanged LLM usage statement, which moves from F to L; there is no extensive rewriting or reorganization of the main paper.

P2.justification: v5 adds Tables 6–11 and Figures 9–11, substantially expanding the visual presentation of comparisons, failures, masking choices, and distractor scenarios. Existing Figure 8 and Table 3 exchange order, while the main figures and original result displays are retained with limited formatting changes.

improvement.justification: The CFG comparison and masking-failure tests address useful gaps in v3's validation, while the LIBERO-90 evaluation supplies evidence under multi-view inputs. These additions make applicability and failure conditions easier to assess. The gain is limited by absent uncertainty estimates and incomplete settings for several new experiments, and the proposed explanation for CFG degradation remains conjectural.
